San Francisco Imposes 45-Day Data Center Moratorium
On Friday,
Mayor
Daniel Lurie
signed a 45-day moratorium, directing the San Francisco Planning Department to assess the effects of data centers and develop regulatory controls.
On X, he said, "San Francisco is the national leader in innovation, and that innovation is one important driver of our city’s recovery. We can never take that position for granted."

Lurie added that the city would spend the next 45 days developing a data center framework that “allows for the technology infrastructure our hospitals, office buildings, academic institutions, and government rely on while prioritizing community needs, keeping electricity rates low, and protecting the clean water and air our residents deserve.”
Today I signed the data center moratorium legislation.

The Board of Supervisors unanimously approved the measure, introduced by Supervisor
Shamann Walton
, last week. Board President
Rafael Mandelman
expedited its consideration, the San Francisco Standard reported.
The signing deadline was Friday. Under the ordinance, the moratorium would have taken effect even without the mayor’s signature.

Walton has raised concerns about the city’s zoning rules, arguing that they lack a clear definition of data centers. He has noted the need to understand how these facilities affect local communities.

AI Data Center Backlash Emerges As Midterm Election Issue
The growing backlash against data centers is emerging as an issue ahead of the U.S. midterm elections. Last month, the Senate blocked the
Ratepayer Protection Act
in a 57-43 vote, falling short of the 60-vote threshold.
